title: Risk Management for Regulated Firms
summary: A ten-module programme giving risk professionals the tools to design, run and evidence a risk management framework that informs decisions and withstands supervisory scrutiny.
intro: This training programme equips risk professionals in regulated firms to design and run a risk management framework that informs decisions, satisfies the board and stands up to supervisory scrutiny, taught by former supervisors.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip risk managers and senior staff with a practical understanding of how an effective risk management framework is built, operated and evidenced in a regulated firm. Participants leave able to set and monitor risk appetite, assess capital and liquidity needs, run stress tests and report risk in a way that drives board decisions.
sections.What It Covers: The three lines model, risk appetite frameworks, risk identification and taxonomy, operational risk and risk and control self-assessment, capital and liquidity self-assessment, stress testing, emerging risks including AI, cyber and climate, risk management information and reporting, and the role of the CRO and the board.
Intended Audience: Chief risk officers, heads of risk and risk managers in regulated firms
Risk analysts and operational risk staff developing their framework and reporting skills
Finance, compliance, internal audit and business managers who own or oversee risks
Learning Objectives: Explain how the three lines model allocates responsibility for risk across the firm
Design a risk appetite framework with measurable limits and triggers linked to strategy
Apply risk identification, taxonomy and risk and control self-assessment techniques consistently
Assess the firm's capital and liquidity needs through an internal self-assessment and stress testing
Evaluate emerging risks, including AI, cyber and climate, and build them into the framework
Produce risk reporting that supports board challenge and agree an action plan for the risk function
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines practical frameworks with case studies, group exercises and worked examples, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of risk management, finance or control work in a regulated firm is helpful. No quantitative modelling background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Principles for an Effective Risk Appetite Framework (2013)
Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (BCBS 239) (2013)
Basel Committee, Revisions to the Principles for the Sound Management of Operational Risk (2021)

modules.title: Risk Governance and the Three Lines Model
modules.summary: How responsibility for risk is allocated between the business, the risk and compliance functions and internal audit, and why supervisors look closely at how this works in practice.
objectives: Explain the roles of the first, second and third lines
Assess the independence, authority and resourcing of the risk function
Identify common failures in how the three lines operate in practice
syllabus: Risk ownership in the business and the role of the second line
Internal audit and independent assurance
Risk committees, terms of reference and escalation routes
Where the three lines blur: lessons from supervisory findings

modules.title: Risk Appetite Frameworks
modules.summary: Translating strategy into a risk appetite statement with measurable metrics, limits and triggers that the board approves and management actually uses.
objectives: Design a risk appetite statement linked to the firm's strategy and business plan
Apply quantitative metrics, limits and early warning triggers
Embed risk appetite into decisions, planning and remuneration
syllabus: Risk capacity, appetite, tolerance and limits
Qualitative statements and quantitative metrics
Cascading appetite to business lines and legal entities
Monitoring, breaches and escalation to the board

modules.title: Risk Identification and Taxonomy
modules.summary: Building a complete, consistent picture of the firm's risks through a clear taxonomy, structured identification and a risk register that stays current.
objectives: Design a risk taxonomy suited to the firm's business model
Apply structured techniques to identify current and emerging risks
Maintain a risk register that links risks, controls and owners
syllabus: Principal risk categories and taxonomy design
Top-down and bottom-up risk identification
Risk registers, owners and control mapping
Business model analysis: seeing risk as a supervisor does

modules.title: Operational Risk and Risk and Control Self-Assessment
modules.summary: Managing operational risk through risk and control self-assessment, loss event data, key risk indicators and scenario analysis that produce reliable insight.
objectives: Explain the sources of operational risk and how they crystallise
Design and run a risk and control self-assessment that challenges the business
Apply loss data, key risk indicators and scenario analysis
syllabus: Operational risk events, causes and impacts
Running risk and control self-assessments with credible challenge
Loss event data, near misses and key risk indicators
Control testing and the link to internal audit

modules.title: Capital Adequacy Self-Assessment
modules.summary: How the firm identifies the risks capital must cover, assesses how much capital it needs over and above regulatory minimums, and documents the assessment for the board and supervisor.
objectives: Explain the purpose of an internal capital adequacy self-assessment
Assess capital needed for risks not fully captured by regulatory minimums
Document the assessment in a way the board owns and supervisors can review
syllabus: Regulatory minimums and the case for additional internal capital
Quantifying credit, market, operational and business risk
Capital planning, buffers and the business plan
Common weaknesses supervisors find in self-assessments

modules.title: Liquidity Risk and Wind-Down Planning
modules.summary: Assessing the firm's liquidity needs under normal and stressed conditions, maintaining a contingency funding plan and preparing for an orderly wind-down if needed.
objectives: Explain the sources of liquidity risk in the firm's business model
Assess liquidity adequacy under business-as-usual and stressed conditions
Design a contingency funding plan and an orderly wind-down plan
syllabus: Liquidity risk drivers, metrics and limits
Internal liquidity adequacy self-assessment
Contingency funding plans and early warning indicators
Wind-down planning: triggers, costs and timelines

modules.title: Stress Testing and Reverse Stress Testing
modules.summary: Designing severe but plausible stress scenarios, assessing their impact on capital, liquidity and operations, and using reverse stress testing to find what would break the business model.
objectives: Design stress scenarios proportionate to the firm's risks and size
Assess the impact of stress on capital, liquidity and profitability
Apply reverse stress testing to identify business model vulnerabilities
syllabus: Scenario design: severity, plausibility and relevance
Linking stress results to capital, liquidity and management actions
Reverse stress testing and recovery options
Presenting stress test results to the board

modules.title: Emerging Risks: AI, Cyber and Climate
modules.summary: How the risk function identifies, assesses and monitors emerging risks from artificial intelligence, cyber threats and climate change, and integrates them into the existing framework.
objectives: Identify emerging risks relevant to the firm and its customers
Assess AI, cyber and climate risks using the firm's existing risk tools
Integrate emerging risks into appetite, scenarios and reporting
syllabus: Emerging risk radars and horizon scanning
AI and model risk, cyber threats and third-party dependency
Climate-related physical and transition risks
Expectations of international standard-setters on emerging risks

modules.title: Risk Management Information and Reporting
modules.summary: Building risk reporting that is accurate, timely and decision-useful, from data aggregation to dashboards that tell the board what it needs to know.
objectives: Design risk management information aligned to appetite and principal risks
Apply principles of risk data aggregation and reporting quality
Produce risk reports that support decisions rather than reassure
syllabus: Risk data aggregation, quality and lineage
Dashboards, key risk indicators and trend analysis
Writing the CRO report: insight, judgement and recommendations
Case study: reporting that failed to warn the board

modules.title: The CRO, the Board and Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around the CRO's relationship with the board and risk committee, and a workshop in which participants assess and plan improvements to their own framework.
objectives: Explain the CRO's role, independence and relationship with the board
Evaluate the effectiveness of the firm's risk framework from a supervisor's perspective
Produce a prioritised action plan for the firm's risk management
syllabus: The CRO's mandate, independence and access to the board
The risk committee: challenge, oversight and effectiveness
Seeing the firm the way a supervisor does: a framework self-assessment
Workshop: the risk function's twelve-month action plan

related.title: Compliance Officer Academy
related.summary: A ten-module academy giving compliance officers the tools to run an independent, risk-based compliance function and handle supervisory engagement with confidence.

related.title: Internal Audit in Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving internal auditors the tools to deliver risk-based assurance over the regulatory risks that matter most to boards and supervisors.

related.title: Internal Investigations and Interviewing Skills
related.summary: A nine-module programme giving control functions a structured method to investigate misconduct, whistleblowing reports and breaches, interview witnesses and subjects, and report findings.

related.title: Management and Leadership for Compliance and Risk Teams
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving managers of compliance, risk and financial crime teams the skills to lead the second line, influence the business and earn the board's confidence.

related.title: Professional Judgement and Core Skills for Compliance Staff
related.summary: A ten-module programme building the judgement, questioning, advisory and writing skills that compliance, risk and financial crime staff need to be trusted by the business, the board and the regulator.

related.title: Terrorist and Proliferation Financing Controls for Firms
related.summary: A nine-module programme equipping firms to assess, detect and report terrorist and proliferation financing, including screening, targeted financial sanctions and dual-use goods red flags.
